findings.where: First screen, the row of five outlined pills under the lead (PPP Law, Infrastructure, Development banks, Governments, Risk allocation), at both widths
findings.fault: The pills are static (parts.txt p10–p14), but they are drawn as outlined capsules with their own boxes, in the same semibold sans and white-on-blue as the action, and they sit just above it. They look like filter chips or links to topic pages, and a click does nothing. They take the shape reserved for selectable chips and buttons.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who clicks 'PPP Law' or 'Risk allocation' to read Mark's work on it gets nothing, and the dead click makes them doubt the site's other links. It also gives the first screen five things that look clickable when the brief asks for one action.

findings.where: First screen, the address button 'Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com →' (parts.txt p16)
findings.fault: The page's one action links to '#', not to a mailto: for the address it shows. Clicking it does nothing. The nav links are stand-ins, but this address and where it goes are known.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks the button to write to Mark gets no mail window and has to copy the address by hand. The founder, testing the hero as a visitor would, finds the one action dead.

findings.where: First screen, the blue field's diagonal hatching, at both widths; against the Texture specimen below the fold
findings.fault: The whole field is covered in fine diagonal stripes, but the Texture specimen says 'No texture: one flat field, no grain and no gradient' and shows a flat field. The tile contradicts itself on one of the three things the brief asks to get right, how busy the ground is. The hatching also reads like a draughtsman's section fill, the techy look the brief rules out.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the hero first, reads one ground in the hero and is told another in the specimen, so neither can be approved. Mark, who is not an engineer, would object to a ground that looks like a technical drawing.

findings.where: First screen, the ghost 'PPP' letters behind the heading (desktop, behind lines 1–3; phone, a cropped 'PP' at the right edge)
findings.fault: Huge pale letters run through the heading's own letters, so the heading's first lines sit on a muddied ground. On a phone they are cropped into stray shapes. This adds a second display element to a screen the research says should be one very large line, and it makes 'PPP' louder than Mark's words.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for refined and not gimmicky. A reader whose eye catches the ghost shapes before the line starts. On a phone, the cut-off letters look like a rendering fault.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the list bullets, and the 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' link with its underline (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: An orange-red appears that is in no part of the stated palette. The palette section says 'Four colours and no accent' and gives house blue as the link colour, yet the article's one link and its bullets are orange-red. Mark's article pages leave the house colours.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for every tile to be built in or around blue #0070C0 and grey #404040. Angélique, who would not know which link colour is right when she adds articles.

findings.where: Article page specimen: the photo caption, the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?', and the three-item list
findings.fault: The vertical rhythm breaks exactly where the brief said it must hold. The caption sits almost on top of the next subhead, with less space than the gap between paragraphs, so the subhead looks like part of the caption. The list items are set solid at a much tighter leading than the 19/30 body, so the wrapped items crowd together. The list then runs straight into a hairline and a link with no gap.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because round 1's critics required this specimen to prove the type rhythm survives an image, a caption, a list and a subhead. Angélique, whose added images and lists will look this cramped on every article. A reader, who loses the subhead as a section start.

findings.where: Article page specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' row under the list
findings.fault: The PDF lecture link hangs directly off the end of the article, separated only by a hairline, with no label or space. It reads as a fourth list item or a stray footnote, not as a related lecture or the PDF list.
findings.who_objects: A reader finishing the article, who cannot tell whether the link belongs to this post or is a separate lecture. The founder, for whom the PDF list is 'the product' and should read as its own group.

findings.fault: The portrait is stacked above the heading, so the first phone screen is the lockup, the nav and a passport-style head shot. Mark's line starts at the very bottom, and the address is a full screen further down.
findings.who_objects: A bank officer arriving on a phone from LinkedIn sees a photo with no message or way to reach him until they scroll. On desktop, the line and the action lead.

findings.where: First screen lockup and the Texture specimen: the aqueduct mark in white
findings.fault: The mark is used as a white reversed version, which the client does not hold (the brand sheet lists only the full-colour JPEG). The house rule makes a new logo version only with the client's yes.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose logo is altered without his say. The founder, who must clear the reversed version with him before this tile can lead.

findings.fault: The 'Source Sans 3' sample sits far lower than the Gelasio display line. It aligns with neither its top nor its baseline, so the two halves of the pair look like they have slipped apart rather than been set side by side.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing the two faces, and any designer reading the tile: the pair looks misplaced rather than composed.
